listingProbePromptVerbatim: Look at the list of available skills/slash-commands in your context. Reply with ONLY a comma-separated list of their names, or NONE if no skills are listed.

fixtureSkill.note: Real ~/.pi/agent/skills and ~/.agents/skills also contribute to what a leak would show (real, not-modified user-level skill dirs) — snapshot at scripts/hell-heaven-bench/harness-probes/runs/pi-real-discovery.snapshot.json. --no-skills is expected to suppress discovery from ALL of these paths, not just the fixture.

sandboxSetup.note: pi has no --cd/-C flag; cwd was set per-invocation via `cd <dir> && pi ...` (the Bash tool resets cwd between calls, so this was repeated on every invocation). Real ~/.pi was only ever read for version/help/list-models probing, never written to by these runs beyond pi's own normal session-history bookkeeping (default session store, not a config mutation).

partA_argvOrderLandmine.verdict: NOT REPRODUCED on 0.82.1. Both the documented-broken order (--no-skills immediately before -p) and the documented-safe order suppressed correctly in every run (6/6 total, 0 leaks). Caveat: small n (3 each) and a model/version double-change vs the original record (harness 0.80.10→0.82.1 AND model — the original argv-order finding did not pin a model). Read as 'did not trigger it in 6 tries under the new conditions', not a certified fix. compilePi's 'emit tail args first' mitigation was NOT tested for removability here (that edit belongs to the other agent working skill-heaven); this result is evidence for that decision, not the decision itself.

partB_discoveryRaceRequantified.docClaim: docs/labs/harness-capability-matrix.md P1: '--no-skills verified live but intermittent: 2 of ~9 floor runs still listed all skills' (~22%, harness 0.80.10, no model pinned in the record).
partB_discoveryRaceRequantified.method: Held argv order FIXED at the documented-safe shape (order B above) across all N runs, so any NONE-vs-listing variance is attributable to the discovery race alone, not the argv-order landmine. N chosen per the brief's instruction to pick a defensible bounded count, not chase a publication-grade estimate.
partB_discoveryRaceRequantified.runsIncluded: orderB-run1..3 + race-run04..15 (12 more), all identical argv shape

confidenceInterval.method: Clopper-Pearson-style upper bound for 0 successes in n trials: 1 - (alpha/2)^(1/n), alpha=0.05 (two-sided 95%); cross-checked against the rule-of-three approximation (3/n)

partB_discoveryRaceRequantified.honestReading: 0/15 is NOT strong evidence the race is fixed: the 95% upper confidence bound (~22%) sits right on top of the previously-recorded ~22% (2/9) rate, so this result is statistically consistent with either 'still races at ~22%' or 'race is now much rarer/fixed' — 15 runs cannot distinguish those. Per B3 (no determinism), this is reported as an interval, not a point estimate. A genuine confound: the model changed (google-antigravity/gemini-3.6-flash vs whatever the original P1 record used), and if the race's window is sensitive to response/scan timing, a different model's latency profile could shift the observed rate independent of any harness fix between 0.80.10 and 0.82.1. Mitigation recommendation (per the brief, not implemented here — another agent owns skill-heaven): floor runs should still assert the listing probe returns NONE and discard/retry leaked runs; this data does not license removing that guard.
